title: TLI Light Palettes
heading: Four light palettes
lede: Four light palettes for transformativeleaders.us. Each keeps Federal navy (#182E56) as ink, so TLI stays in the New Statecraft family while moving off the Institute's warm paper and dark navy bands.
footnote: Every text color is held to WCAG AAA (7:1) against what it sits on: section headline, body and accent on each section background, and card headline, body and accent on every background of every card theme; buttons reach 3:1 on their card and their labels 7:1. The lightest tints stay at least ΔE 5 from the Institute's paper (#F6F3EC) so TLI doesn't read as the same site; the Institute itself stays on that warm paper with ink monochrome text, and none of these reuse it. Contrast is calculated live from the hex values.
brand_sub: New Statecraft's logo colors. Every palette below is checked against them for hue harmony.

sample.heading: Change the incentives that drive Washington.

cards.p: Invites congressional candidates from both parties — or no party — to commit to competitive elections, fiscal responsibility, and accountable institutions.
Recognizes federal lawmakers who champion the Accord's agenda for reform during a two-year term of Congress.

section_uses: Lightest band: intro copy, the Accord list, long-form reading.
Middle band: card grids and forms. Cards below sit on it.
Deepest cool band: Join the movement, replacing a dark navy band.
comp_uses: Warm counterpoint to Section 1: the Accord framework and long copy.
Warm mid band: the Scorecard or a pull quote.
Deepest warm band: Support the Initiative and donation strip.
stack_sub: Cool and warm alternate the way the TLI page runs: intro, Initiative cards, Accord, Scorecard, Join the movement, Support.

stack.p: We firmly believe that much of the current dysfunction in Congress can be fixed by electing and empowering a critical mass of lawmakers willing to put country before party.

stack.h: A framework for practical governance reforms.
stack.p: Citizens' trust in government has collapsed and restoring it will require fundamental changes.
The inaugural Scorecard will be published in 2028, at the conclusion of the next session of Congress.
Leaders and citizens across the country are uniting behind a better way forward.
Help fund strategic outreach to all congressional candidates.

palettes.name: 1 · Capitol Mist
palettes.sub: Cool blue-gray paper and pale slate section areas, Federal navy ink, logo red buttons. The most direct light inversion of the navy scheme: same hue family, flipped value.
palettes.red_name: CTA red (logo red, ½ step darker)
palettes.mood: Cool blue-gray paper and pale slate sections with Federal navy ink and logo red buttons: the most direct light inversion of the Institute's navy scheme, the same family with its values flipped. Wheat and sand tints warm the second half of the page.
palettes.tech: Sections 1–3 are the cool blue-gray, lightest to deepest (#F4F6FA to #CCD6E5). Sections 4–6 are wheat and sand at hue 37°, the complement of the 219° ink.
palettes.harmony: area, ink and accent all within 11° of Logo blue (same family); CTA on Logo red's hue

palettes.name: 2 · Limestone
palettes.comp_name: Clay and terracotta, the complement of the navy accents
palettes.sub: Near-neutral cool stone, like the Capitol's limestone in shade, with a pale blue-gray third section for contrast. Navy ink and accents carry all the color. Section 1 leans just cool enough (#F3F6F8) and Section 2 a touch deeper (#E5E6E2) to stay clearly apart from the Institute's warm cream (ΔE 5+) without going blue.
palettes.mood: Near-neutral cool stone, like the Capitol's limestone in shade, with a pale blue-gray third section for contrast. Navy ink and accents carry all the color, and clay and terracotta tints warm the second half.
palettes.tech: Section 1 leans just cool enough (#F3F6F8) and Section 2 a touch deeper (#E5E6E2) to stay ΔE 5+ from the Institute's warm cream without going blue. Sections 4–6 are clay tints at hue 25°, the complement of the navy.
palettes.harmony: ink and accent within 11° of Logo blue (same family); CTA within 1° of Logo red

palettes.mood: Capitol Mist with red added the way public buildings carry it: brick, not blush. Cool blue-gray paper and slate, a brick-red accent, a baked-clay tint, and one deep brick band for Join the movement, so the red reads solid, civic and a little weathered rather than soft.
palettes.tech: Sections 1–3 are Capitol Mist's cool blue-gray (#F4F6FA to #CCD6E5). The reds stay dark and earthy, hue 25–30° like the logo red, never the pink range: accent #722420 holds AAA on every light section, and the deep brick band #682321 takes white text at 11:1. The light warm tints stay wheat (#F9EEDC) and baked clay (#E5D1B8, a sandy tan at hue 72°), because a light tint of red itself reads pink.
palettes.harmony: ink within 11° of Logo blue (same family); accent, deep brick and CTA on Logo red's hue
palettes.stack_sub: Cool and warm alternate as in Capitol Mist; the deep brick band carries Join the movement, and Support moves to the baked clay so the red button keeps its contrast.

mood.words: civic, institutional, serious and trustworthy, rooted in Federal navy and the materials of public buildings (limestone, marble, granite, bronze, parchment, official seals): muted, dusty and greyed tones with navy and logo-red anchors; never pastel, candy, blush, lavender or playful
